assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 30,000 operations/s at peak with an 8.5:1 read:write ratio — everybody checks the board, far fewer post a score. A tournament finish inverts this briefly and the submit path is what has to absorb it.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: The live ranking IS the Redis sorted set — ZADD on submit, ZREVRANGE for the top-N, ZREVRANK for a player's position. The engine charges every one of those the same flat ~90,000 ops/s per node, which is wrong in a specific direction: a top-10 read is cheap, and a deep ZRANGE over a large window is not. The engine has no data-structure cost model.

assumptions.subject: cache_ha
assumptions.statement: 2 Redis nodes are modelled as 2x capacity. That is honest for the READ path (a replica serves reads) and over-credits the WRITE path, because every ZADD must land on the primary. At the modelled 3,000 submits/s a single primary is comfortable, so the distortion does not change the verdict here — but it would at 10x the write rate.

assumptions.subject: q
assumptions.statement: Scores go to a durable log BEFORE the sorted set, so an in-memory ranking can be rebuilt after a Redis loss. Without this the leaderboard is only as durable as one Redis process — the single most common way this design fails in production.

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: Postgres is the system of record and the source for rebuilds; it is deliberately OFF the hot read path (visit_prob 0.05, only for players absent from the cached window). Serving ranks from SQL with an ORDER BY over millions of rows is the design this blueprint exists to replace.

assumptions.subject: worker
assumptions.statement: The materialiser recomputes windowed boards (daily / weekly / seasonal) and writes them back. Sized at ~500 events/s per instance with a ~30 ms batch step; real cost depends entirely on how many windows and segments you maintain.

assumptions.subject: fairness
assumptions.statement: Anti-cheat, score validation and tie-breaking are not modelled. They are where leaderboard projects actually spend their engineering time, and they add per-submission work this capacity model does not charge for.

_library.summary: A Redis sorted set serves live rankings while a durable score log keeps it rebuildable.
